doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: What Hyman listens to, including Richard Strauss
summary: He listens to a lot of music, mostly classical, and admires Strauss.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Do you listen to music as much as let’s say, a non-musician who loves music? Do you spend a lot of time listening to music still?
Yes. I do listen to a lot of music.
Sometimes musicians themselves seem to maybe not listen as much because it’s like their job every day.

Well, yeah, no I like to listen to — I don’t necessarily listen to a great deal of jazz, although a fair amount of that, but I like to listen to classical music. We have a local public radio station in Florida that does a wide variety of stuff. But if I have my own inclination, tapes I might put in the car to play, it might be Richard Strauss in particular.
Strauss was wonderful. He went absolutely as far as you can go without jettisoning the whole idea of tonality.
